bifrost: springboard/src/shell/share/mod.rs (share sheet, closest hand-off counterpart); springboard/sdk/src/share.rs (SDK share); no mail app or mail extension point
summary: MailKit is an extension point for Apple's Mail app: content blockers, message actions, compose-window handlers and S/MIME or PGP security handlers all plug into Mail. BifrOSt has no Mail app and no mail extension host, so the framework has no counterpart. The only nearby piece is the share sheet, which hands text and files to registered apps; it does not reach a mail compose window.

features.note: There is no host Mail app to load an extension into. Nothing in springboard/apps or springboard/sdk/src implements mail extension points.
No mail message viewer exists. The browser has no content-rule or tracker blocking either, which is a separate gap for web content.
No mail download pipeline or message store exists in BifrOSt.

features.feature: Compose window handling and recipient annotation
features.note: No compose window for mail. Notes has a compose screen (springboard/apps/notes-desktop/src/notes/mod.rs) for notes, not mail.
No S/MIME or PGP support. The keychain (springboard/src/keychain.rs) stores secrets but does no message signing or encryption.
No mail message type exists. Contacts (springboard/apps/contacts-desktop) hold people, not messages.
Depends on the Mail extension host, which BifrOSt does not have.

features.feature: Hand text and files to a mail compose window
features.apple: Mail as a system share service (outside MailKit)
features.note: Mailto addresses with cc, bcc, subject and body, percent-encoded, and attachment paths are tested headless in springboard/ui/tests/parity_sdk-gaps-01.rs. Mail opens a mailto: link through the shell URL routing (manifest schemes = ["mailto"]), and bifrost_app::mail_compose::compose hands a draft to it. Files travel as read grants (the mail_compose service grants each one to Mail, which attaches it); a file named by path is refused. Not verified on Midget.

gaps: No mail app and no mail data layer (accounts, IMAP/SMTP, mailboxes), so there is nothing for a mail extension to extend.
No message-level content blocking (rules applied when a message is displayed); the browser has no equivalent either.
No S/MIME or PGP signing and decryption API in the SDK.
The share sheet has no mail target, so a text or file cannot be handed to a compose window.
